meta.title: MiniMax-M3
meta.description: MiniMax M3 vision-language MoE (427B total / 26B active) for frontier coding, agent toolchains, and 1M-token reasoning via MSA sparse attention — native multimodal (image + video + computer use); BF16 plus MXFP8, NVIDIA Blackwell NVFP4, and AMD MI355X MXFP4 variants. Runs on NVIDIA (Hopper/Blackwell) and AMD CDNA4/CDNA3.
meta.performance_headline: Frontier coding and agent (SWE-Bench Pro 59.0, Terminal-Bench 2.1 66.0); MSA sparse attention; 1M context

recommended_command.docker_command:
docker run --gpus all \
  --privileged --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
  -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m3 MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --max-model-len 65536 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3

strategy_spec.name: single_node_tp
strategy_spec.description: Single-node tensor parallel. Splits the model across all local GPUs. TP size is set to the GPU count at deploy time. The simplest multi-GPU strategy — works for all model architectures.

hardware_profile.description: NVIDIA H200 SXM 141 GB HBM3e · 8-GPU HGX node

pip.command:
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -U vllm --pre \
  --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/cu130 \
  --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130 \
  --index-strategy unsafe-best-match
pip.note: vLLM 0.24.0 isn't released yet — nightly required.

tool_calling.description: MiniMax M3 tool call parser with automatic tool choice

reasoning.description: MiniMax M3 reasoning parser (supports `thinking` and `non-thinking` modes, switchable per request)

spec_decoding.description: Eagle3 speculative decoding with an Inferact MiniMax-M3 draft head — accelerates decoding. Choose between the standard MHA head and the GQA head (16× smaller draft KV cache — better for long-context or high-batch deployments).

eagle3.label: MHA
eagle3.description: Standard Eagle3 draft head (Multi-Head Attention, 64 KV heads).

eagle3_gqa.label: GQA
eagle3_gqa.description: GQA Eagle3 draft head (Grouped Query Attention, 4 KV heads vs 64) — 16× smaller draft KV cache. Prefer for long-context or large-batch deployments where draft KV memory is the constraint.

text_only.description: Skip loading the vision encoder for text-only workloads — frees VRAM for KV cache. Mutually exclusive with encoder_parallel.

thinking_always_on.description: Pin `thinking_mode: enabled` server-side — every turn reasons before answering, including after tool results. Recommended for agentic workflows.

encoder_parallel.description: Run the vision encoder data-parallel instead of tensor-parallel — avoids TP comm overhead on the small encoder. Also enables the host-shared-memory multimodal processor cache and the per-brand encoder attention backend (FlashInfer on NVIDIA, AITER FlashAttention on AMD). Mutually exclusive with text_only.

default.description: Native BF16 checkpoint — multi-node TP recommended for long-context headroom

mxfp8.description: NVIDIA-quantized MXFP8 weights — Blackwell (B200/B300) for native MX tensor cores, and AMD CDNA4 (MI350X/MI355X, gfx950) for native MXFP8 Matrix Cores.

nvfp4.description: NVIDIA-quantized NVFP4 weights (ModelOpt) for Blackwell (B200/B300/GB200) — native FP4 tensor cores, ~half the VRAM of MXFP8.

mxfp4.description: AMD Quark OCP MXFP4 weights and dynamic MXFP4 activations for MI355X (gfx950).

h200_agentx.label: AgentX TP8
h200_agentx.description: One 8-GPU H200 node, TP8, with the GQA EAGLE3 draft (three tokens) and thinking always on; the scheduler batch is twice the concurrency.
h200_agentx.runbook:
The H200 AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`minimaxm3-fp8-h200-vllm-agentic-mtp`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4429](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4429)) serves the MXFP8 checkpoint with the GQA EAGLE3 draft (three speculative tokens) as one aggregated vLLM worker on a single 8-GPU H200 node: TP8, no expert parallelism, no host KV offload.

The InferenceX throughput points replaced block verification with synthetic rejection at the committed golden EAGLE3-GQA acceptance length (2.78 for MiniMax-M3 with three draft tokens, thinking on; [`minimaxm3_eagle3_gqa.yaml`](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/inferencex-e2e/infx/golden_al_distribution/minimaxm3_eagle3_gqa.yaml)) so every point is measured at the same acceptance rate. The command above does not set it.

b200_agentx.label: AgentX TP4
b200_agentx.description: TP4 on four of the node's eight B200 GPUs with the GQA EAGLE3 draft (three tokens, local argmax reduction); the larger points add host KV offload.
b200_agentx.runbook:
The B200 AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`minimaxm3-fp4-b200-vllm-agentic-mtp` and `minimaxm3-fp4-b200-vllm-agentic-mtp-c10`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4382](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4382)) serves the NVFP4 checkpoint with the GQA EAGLE3 draft as one aggregated vLLM worker on a single 8-GPU B200 node. Most points run TP4; the concurrency-10 arm also has a TP8 point.

The host-KV-offload points pin 1,073 GB of host memory for KV blocks across the node (lazy offload).

The **Verified** badge for this GPU is recipe-wide. This preset covers the NVFP4 variant only; the GQA draft override in `features.spec_decoding` also applies to the other variants on this GPU, which were not qualified.

The InferenceX throughput points replaced block verification with synthetic rejection at the committed golden EAGLE3-GQA acceptance length so every point is measured at the same acceptance rate. Production serving keeps the default rejection sampler, as in the command above.

b200_agentx_c10.label: AgentX active-seq caps
b200_agentx_c10.description: Caps the sequences the scheduler keeps active (--max-num-active-seqs) well below the concurrency, with a five- or three-token GQA draft without local argmax reduction.
b200_agentx_c10.runbook:
The B200 AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`minimaxm3-fp4-b200-vllm-agentic-mtp` and `minimaxm3-fp4-b200-vllm-agentic-mtp-c10`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4382](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4382)) serves the NVFP4 checkpoint with the GQA EAGLE3 draft as one aggregated vLLM worker on a single 8-GPU B200 node. Most points run TP4; the concurrency-10 arm also has a TP8 point.

The **Verified** badge for this GPU is recipe-wide. This preset covers the NVFP4 variant only; the GQA draft override in `features.spec_decoding` also applies to the other variants on this GPU, which were not qualified.

The InferenceX throughput points replaced block verification with synthetic rejection at the committed golden EAGLE3-GQA acceptance length so every point is measured at the same acceptance rate. Production serving keeps the default rejection sampler, as in the command above.

b300_agentx.label: AgentX
b300_agentx.description: One B300 node: TP8 at concurrency 1, TP4 at 20 and 24, TP2 with host KV offload at 24 and 28; GQA EAGLE3 draft (three tokens, local argmax reduction).
b300_agentx.runbook:
The B300 AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`minimaxm3-fp4-b300-vllm-agentic-mtp`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4357](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4357)) serves the NVFP4 checkpoint with the GQA EAGLE3 draft (three speculative tokens) as one aggregated vLLM worker on a single B300 node: TP8 at concurrency 1, TP4 at concurrency 20 and 24, and TP2 at 24 and 28 with host KV offload.

The TP2 points pin 749 GB of host memory for KV blocks (lazy offload).

The **Verified** badge for this GPU is recipe-wide. This preset covers the NVFP4 variant only; the GQA draft override in `features.spec_decoding` also applies to the other variants on this GPU, which were not qualified.

The InferenceX throughput points replaced block verification with synthetic rejection at the committed golden EAGLE3-GQA acceptance length (2.78 for MiniMax-M3 with three draft tokens, thinking on; [`minimaxm3_eagle3_gqa.yaml`](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/inferencex-e2e/infx/golden_al_distribution/minimaxm3_eagle3_gqa.yaml)) so every point is measured at the same acceptance rate. The command above does not set it.

mi355x_agentx.label: AgentX
mi355x_agentx.description: MXFP4 with the GQA EAGLE3 draft (three tokens), thinking on and no offload; TP4 enables the pinned image's monokernel, while TP2 uses ordinary decode.
mi355x_agentx.runbook:
This opt-in MXFP4 profile follows [InferenceX #4418](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4418)
at `f10885621773d1f900b6b4d002ee37863e583af3`: the
[`agg-variants.yaml` SRT bundle](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/f10885621773d1f900b6b4d002ee37863e583af3/inferencex-e2e/benchmarks/single_node/srt-slurm-recipes/minimaxm3/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agg-variants.yaml)
for `minimaxm3-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-mtp`. It serves
[`amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4) on one
MI355X node, text-only, with no expert parallelism, model offload or KV offload.
Both TP4 and TP2 use Model Runner V2; every point sets `max-num-seqs` to twice
its client concurrency. INT4 QuickReduce, FP8 KV/indexer caches, the 0.9 memory
fraction and the 128-token graph limit are specific to this workload.

TP4 enables the [pinned `df6603f` monokernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/df6603f0583375f244d1ac6d36265462b7490392/vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/specialized_decode/runtime/spec.py).
It handles supported physical decode widths 1–16 with EAGLE3 K3; larger or
mixed steps fall back to ordinary decode. TP2 omits `--monokernel` because
this implementation requires TP4. The profile reproduces that image, not
later monokernel implementations or general MiniMax-M3 defaults.

[Source run 39890471932](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39890471932)
contains the twelve throughput points and their real-verification evals.
The audited head's bound serving configurations match that run's source.
[Reuse run 40416678647](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/40416678647)
skipped the GPU matrices; it is not a fresh qualification. The earlier
[#2959 baseline](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34609443618/attempts/2)
does not qualify this image or monokernel. Performance is reported by
InferenceX; local recipe validation does not reproduce GPU performance.

Ordinary serving and accuracy evaluation retain real target verification.
Throughput reproduction alone adds the following keys to `--speculative-config`:

```json
{"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":2.78}
```

The [golden 2.78 acceptance length](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/f10885621773d1f900b6b4d002ee37863e583af3/inferencex-e2e/infx/golden_al_distribution/minimaxm3_eagle3_gqa.yaml)
is for the three-token GQA draft with thinking enabled. Synthetic rejection
bypasses real verification; never use it for users or accuracy evals.
AgentX's `AIPERF_APPLY_CHAT_TEMPLATE=true` and required `vllm:` metrics prefix
are benchmark-client settings, not server flags. The source's
`dram-utilization: 0.20` is orchestration metadata, not KV offload.

guide:
## Overview

[MiniMax-M3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3) is a frontier
vision-language MoE model from [MiniMax](https://www.minimax.io/).

- **MSA (MiniMax Sparse Attention)** — scalable sparse-attention architecture
  that lifts the context window to **1M tokens**. MiniMax reports per-token
  compute at 1M context reduced to ~1/20 of the previous generation, with
  >9× prefill and >15× decode speedup vs dense baselines.
- **Frontier coding and agent capabilities** — SWE-Bench Pro 59.0%,
  Terminal-Bench 2.1 66.0%, SWE-fficiency 34.8%, KernelBench Hard 28.8%,
  MCP Atlas 74.2%.
- **Native multimodal** — image + video inputs, plus computer-use; trained
  multimodally from step 0.
- **Two reasoning modes** — `thinking` (complex reasoning / agents) and
  `non-thinking` (latency-sensitive), switchable per request.

## Prerequisites

- **OS:** Linux
- **Python:** 3.10 - 3.13
- **NVIDIA:** compute capability >= 9.0 (Hopper) recommended; 8x H200 / H20
  for a tight single-node BF16 fit, or multi-node TP for long-context headroom
- **AMD:** MI350X/MI355X (gfx950), MI300X/MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2+. BF16
  needs TP=8; the MXFP8 variant runs from TP=4.
- **`--block-size 128` is mandatory on every platform** (MSA sparse/index cache).

### Docker (NVIDIA)

MiniMax-M3 support has not yet shipped in a stable vLLM release — use the
dedicated Docker image:

```bash
docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m3
```

### Docker (AMD ROCm)

Use the nightly image, which is the image the AMD variants of this recipe pin:

```bash
docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly
```

```bash
docker run --rm -it --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --group-add video \
  --cap-add SYS_PTRACE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --ipc=host \
  --shm-size=16g -p 8000:8000 \
  --entrypoint /bin/bash \
  vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly
```

## Launching the Server

### NVIDIA — TP8 (8x H200 / H20)

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

#### TP8 + Expert Parallel

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --block-size 128 \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

#### DP8 + Expert Parallel

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --block-size 128 \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

### AMD ROCm (MI350X/MI355X (gfx950), MI300X/MI325X (gfx942))

On AMD MI300X / MI325X / MI355X, run with CUDA graphs and set the following
before any of the serve commands below. It avoids the MiniMax-M3 decode breakable-cudagraph path that would
otherwise force eager execution (per @hongxiayang):

```bash
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0
```

For gfx950: Prefer using the MXFP8 variant `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` for TP=4 and a smaller
footprint. Use TP=8 for lower latency or long context length, or the default bf16 model.

#### TP8 (Text or Vision)

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

Add the vision-encoder flags (`--mm-encoder-tp-mode data
--mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA`) for multimodal serving.

#### TP8 + `--quantization fp8_per_channel`

Online **per-channel FP8 (PTPC)** quantization of the BF16 checkpoint halves the
weight footprint (≈100 → **≈50 GiB/GPU**, ~1.75× more KV cache) and lifts
batched throughput with **gsm8k unchanged from BF16** (lossless); 
These env vars and the flag are for the **BF16 checkpoint only**.

```bash
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0

vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --quantization fp8_per_channel \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

#### TP8 + Expert Parallel

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --block-size 128 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

#### DP8 + Expert Parallel

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --block-size 128 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

## FP8 KV Cache

Add `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` to any command for ~1.5× the KV pool — lossless
in our testing across the full native context. Especially worth it for high
concurrency or long context, where KV is the binding constraint.

## Context Length & GPU Memory

The full **1M-token** window (`context_length: 1048576`) needs a large KV
cache. To save GPU memory, you can optionally cap the context with
`--max-model-len`:

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --max-model-len 131072        # 128K instead of the full 1M
```

AMD ROCm notes: Native context is 512K. To go past it, supply a YaRN rope_scaling on the text config
(a top-level override silently misses the decoder's config) and allow the long max length.
TP=8 + fp8 KV is the practical combo at 1M:

```bash
VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 \
  vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"rope_scaling":{"rope_type":"yarn","factor":2.0,"original_max_position_embeddings":524288}}}'
```

- Set `--max-model-len` to the longest prompt + output you actually serve
  (e.g. `32768`, `131072`, `262144`). A smaller window frees KV-pool headroom
  for higher concurrency and lets the model fit on fewer GPUs; if you need the
  full 1M window, consider scaling out with multi-node TP instead.

## Client Usage

Recommended sampling parameters (from the model card):

- `temperature = 1.0`
- `top_p = 0.95`
- `top_k = 40`

Default system prompt:

```
You are a helpful assistant. Your name is MiniMax-M3 and is built by MiniMax.
```

Example chat request:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3",
    "temperature": 1.0,
    "top_p": 0.95,
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant. Your name is MiniMax-M3 and is built by MiniMax."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "Explain MSA sparse attention in 3 bullets."}
    ]
  }'
```

## Thinking Modes

M3 reasoning is controlled by the `thinking_mode`, there are three values:

- **`enabled`** — the model thinks before every response, including after tool results. 
  Use for complex reasoning and agents.
- **`disabled`** — no thinking; the model answers directly. Use for
  latency-sensitive turns.
- **`adaptive`** *(default when unset)* — the model decides whether to think
  based on the task.

Pass it per request through `chat_template_kwargs`. The same value also tunes
the `minimax_m3` reasoning parser, so `reasoning` and `content` are
split correctly in every mode.

```python

# Start the MiniMax-M3 model by referring to the command above first.

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(api_key="EMPTY", base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1")

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Prove there are infinitely many primes."}],
    extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking_mode": "enabled"}},
)
msg = response.choices[0].message
print(msg.reasoning)  # the <mm:think> block
print(msg.content)  # the final answer
```

## Benchmarking

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend vllm \
  --model MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input 2048 \
  --random-output 1024 \
  --max-concurrency 10 \
  --num-prompt 100
```

## Quantized Variant (MXFP8)

[`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8`](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8)
is an MXFP8 checkpoint quantized by NVIDIA from the original FP16 weights —
roughly half the VRAM of the BF16 release. Select the **mxfp8** variant above,
or pass the repo id directly to `vllm serve`:

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

For best MXFP8 throughput, prefer Blackwell (B200/B300) for native MX tensor cores,
or AMD CDNA4 (MI350X/MI355X, gfx950) for native MXFP8 matrix cores.

On AMD MI300X, the **mxfp8** variant stacks two accuracy-safe scheduling
levers from the InferenceX MI300X tuning recipe and avoids the high-concurrency
expert-parallel regression by using plain TP8:

```bash
export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=0
export TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_HIPBLASLT=1
export NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS="${NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS:-112}"
export GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES="${GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES:-2}"

vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len "$MAX_MODEL_LEN" \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --async-scheduling \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

On AMD MI355X the **mxfp8** variant additionally enables the AITER kernels,
the fused shared-experts MoE, and INT4 QuickReduce, and pulls the nightly ROCm
image (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`) — selected automatically in the command
builder. If you launch by hand:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4

vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

### MXFP8 high-concurrency options on MI355X

The command above is the default serving configuration and is tuned for the
general case. **AITER page-16 sparse paged attention** helps specifically at **long context and
high concurrency**. It maps MiniMax-M3's top-k 128-token MSA blocks onto AITER page-16 block tables
and runs AITER Gluon paged attention over only the selected KV pages.

The high-concurrency configuration is:

```bash
# Long context + high concurrency only (isl >= 8k, conc >= 64). Regresses
# short-context / low-concurrency serving.
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1
export VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=0
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION_MIN_SIZE_KB=256

vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --language-model-only \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --linear-backend emulation \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

Note: Outside the long-context/high-batch
regime the shuffled layout costs more than it saves; leave it at `0`:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=0
```

## Quantized Variant (NVFP4 on Blackwell)

[`nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4)
is an NVFP4 checkpoint quantized by NVIDIA with ModelOpt. It requires a vLLM
build with MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 support (vllm-project/vllm PR #46380).

Select the **nvfp4** variant and **B200** hardware in the command builder, or
launch the tested B200 baseline directly:

```bash
VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high \
  vllm serve nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --block-size 128 \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

Pair it with EAGLE3 speculative decoding (the *Spec decoding* feature) for
faster decode — the validated B200 benchmark runs the NVFP4 target against the
`Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3` draft head (3 speculative tokens):

```bash
VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high \
  vllm serve nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --block-size 128 \
  --language-model-only \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "eagle3", "model": "Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "attention_backend": "FLASH_ATTN"}'
```

For long-context or high-batch workloads where draft KV memory is the binding
constraint, swap in the **GQA** variant:

```bash
VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high \
  vllm serve nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --block-size 128 \
  --language-model-only \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "eagle3", "model": "Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "attention_backend": "FLASH_ATTN"}'
```

You may also consider FlashInfer for draft attention if it performs better for
your workload, and local argmax reduction to reduce communication traffic:

```bash
--speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_local_argmax_reduction":true}'
```

## GB200: InferenceX AgentX aggregated (Dynamo + vLLM)

The GB200 AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`minimaxm3-fp4-gb200-dynamo-vllm-agentic-agg-mtp`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4281](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4281)) serves the NVFP4 checkpoint with the GQA EAGLE3 draft (three speculative tokens) as one aggregated vLLM worker behind the Dynamo frontend's KV-aware router. TP4 runs on one 4-GPU GB200 tray; TP8 spans two trays. Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-5555a2d8f7116b2b4877f66516f4128176cf722a@sha256:8896fd7b29fc4ee7ce839f146cb4757984c476ec79d0234ffa8c995dee6e339a`, Dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261016` (`pip install ai-dynamo==1.6.0.dev20261016`).

In the command builder, pick **GB200** and the **NVFP4** variant (the builder keeps the current variant when you switch hardware, so select NVFP4 explicitly), turn on **Spec Decoding → GQA** and **Text-only**, and use **Single-node TP** for TP4 or **Multi-node TP** with 2 nodes for TP8. That renders the worker flags and environment below as a `vllm serve` command. Direct links: [TP4](https://recipes.vllm.ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3?hardware=gb200&variant=nvfp4&features=tool_calling,reasoning,spec_decoding,text_only&fmode=spec_decoding:eagle3_gqa&strategy=single_node_tp) and [TP8 on two trays](https://recipes.vllm.ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3?hardware=gb200&variant=nvfp4&features=tool_calling,reasoning,spec_decoding,text_only&fmode=spec_decoding:eagle3_gqa&strategy=multi_node_tp&nodes=2). The GB200 **Verified** badge applies to this NVFP4 profile only; the GQA draft and TP8 all-reduce overrides also apply to the other variants on GB200, which were not qualified.

For the host-KV-offload points, don't use the **KV Offload → Simple** pill as is: its budget is fixed at 220 GiB per rank (880 GiB per 4-GPU tray) with `lazy_offload: false`, which is more host memory than a GB200 tray can give KV blocks. Replace its `--kv-transfer-config` with the qualified one below and set `VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD=1`. The per-concurrency settings in this table, the Dynamo KV-router frontend and its services stay in this guide.

| Concurrency | TP | `--max-num-seqs` | Host KV offload | CUDA graph capture sizes |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 2 | none | `1,2,4,8` |
| 1 | 8 | 2 | none | `1,2,4,8` |
| 10 | 4 | 16 | none | `1,2,4` then every 4 up to `64` |
| 20 | 4 | 8 | SimpleCPUOffload | every 4 from `4` to `32` |
| 25 | 4 | 16 | SimpleCPUOffload | every 4 from `4` to `64` |
| 30 | 4 | 45 | SimpleCPUOffload | every 4 from `4` to `180` |

Every list ends with `256,512,1024,2048` and uses `{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[...]}`. Sizes 1 and 2 give the drafter's decode steps full CUDA graphs at concurrency 1.

The InferenceX throughput points replaced block verification with synthetic rejection at the committed golden EAGLE3-GQA acceptance length (2.78 for MiniMax-M3 with three draft tokens, thinking on; [`minimaxm3_eagle3_gqa.yaml`](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/inferencex-e2e/infx/golden_al_distribution/minimaxm3_eagle3_gqa.yaml)) so every point is measured at the same acceptance rate. Production serving keeps the default rejection sampler, as in the command below; the lane's accuracy evals ran that way.

### Services and environment

Start etcd and NATS (JetStream on, 32 MB max payload) once:

```bash
etcd --listen-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379 --advertise-client-urls http://<infra-host>:2379
printf 'max_payload: 33554432\njetstream {}\n' > nats.conf && nats-server -c nats.conf
```

On every worker tray (and on the frontend host, point the same two variables at the services):

```bash
export ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://<infra-host>:2379 NATS_SERVER=nats://<infra-host>:4222
export VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=trtllm
export NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1
export UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,rc
```

Set `UCX_NET_DEVICES` and `NCCL_IB_HCA` to the node's RDMA devices. For TP8 across two trays, use `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=mnnvl` instead of `trtllm`. Loading the 1M-context engine takes a while, so raise `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` and `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` well above their defaults.

### Worker

```bash
python3 -m dynamo.vllm --model nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 --served-model-name nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 \
  --request-plane tcp --device-ids 0,1,2,3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --trust-remote-code \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER","use_trtllm_attention":true,"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8","minimax_m3_msa_decode_backend":"cutlass"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_local_argmax_reduction":true}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs <S> \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[<sizes from the table>,256,512,1024,2048]}' \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --stream-interval 20 --language-model-only \
  --kv-events-config '{"publisher":"zmq","topic":"kv-events","enable_kv_cache_events":true,"endpoint":"tcp://*:5200"}' \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --dyn-reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --dyn-tool-call-parser minimax_m3
```

The pinned nightly predates the `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` spelling (added in vLLM #61479), so this command uses `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`; newer images accept both. The command builder renders the same flag for GB200.

For TP8, run the same command on both trays with `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --nnodes 2 --node-rank <0|1> --master-addr <first-tray-ip>`, adding `--headless` on node rank 1.

For the host-KV-offload points, also set `VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD=1` and add:

```bash
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":777389080576,"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":194347270144,"lazy_offload":true}}'
```

That gives each of the four ranks about 181 GiB of pinned host memory for KV blocks.

### Frontend

```bash
export ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://<infra-host>:2379 NATS_SERVER=nats://<infra-host>:4222 DYN_REQUEST_PLANE=tcp
export DYN_TOKENIZER=fastokens DYN_TOKENIZER_CACHE_BYTES=8589934592 DYN_TCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=60
python3 -m dynamo.frontend --trust-remote-code \
  --router-mode kv --router-kv-events --router-temperature 0 \
  --router-session-affinity-ttl-secs 14400 --kv-cache-block-size 128
```

The KV router uses the workers' KV events to send each request to the worker holding its prefix, and session affinity keeps a conversation on that worker: send a stable conversation ID in the `X-Dynamo-Session-ID` request header. This Dynamo build warns that `--router-temperature` is deprecated and will be removed in v1.7; newer builds take `router_temperature` in the default policy parameters of `--router-policy-config`.

### MXFP4 AgentX on MI355X

The opt-in [AgentX preset](#preset-mi355x_agentx) follows
[InferenceX #4418](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4418) on its
pinned ROCm image: TP4 at concurrency 1, 4, 5, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 24 and 32

the three-token GQA EAGLE3 draft and real target verification, with no offload.

reproduction only, as described in the preset's runbook.

## Troubleshooting

- **`--block-size` mismatch.** MSA's sparse block size is 128; the vLLM KV
  cache block size must match. Using the default (16) misaligns the sparse
  attention indexing (on AMD it crashes with `No common block size for 16`).
- **Parsers.** `--tool-call-parser` and `--reasoning-parser` both use
  `minimax_m3` — distinct from `minimax_m2` used by earlier releases.
- **Long context KV cache.** See *Context Length & GPU Memory* above — cap
  `--max-model-len` or scale to multi-node TP if you OOM.
- **Vision encoder.** The encoder is small, so at high TP the *Encoder
  Parallel* option runs it data-parallel (`--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`) to
  avoid TP comm overhead; it also turns on the vision-encoder attention
  backend (FlashInfer on NVIDIA, `--mm-encoder-attn-backend FLASHINFER`;
  AITER FlashAttention on AMD, `ROCM_AITER_FA`) and the host-shared-memory
  multimodal processor cache (`--mm-processor-cache-type shm`). For **text-only** workloads enable *Text only*
  (`--language-model-only`) to skip loading the encoder and free VRAM — it is
  mutually exclusive with Encoder Parallel.


## EAGLE3 Speculative Decoding

Two Inferact draft heads are available as selectable modes in the *Spec decoding*
feature — both use `method: eagle3` with 3 speculative tokens and share
MiniMax-M3's embedding table and LM head:

| Mode | Repo | KV heads | Draft KV cache |
|------|------|----------|----------------|
| **MHA** (default) | `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3` | 64 | baseline |
| **GQA** | `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA` | 4 | **16× smaller** |

The GQA head uses Grouped Query Attention (4 KV heads grouped from 64 query
heads) — the only architectural difference from the MHA head. The 16× reduction
in draft KV state makes it preferable when draft memory is the binding constraint
(long-context serving or large batch sizes).
